Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy" (#1791)

Issues.Title: Update docs to reflect the status of .NET Standard in 2020
Issues.Body:

Issues.Body:

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: [UWP] HttpClientHandler - Digest Authentication Broken on Windows 10 PC
Issues.Body:
Just recently I found that my UWP app can no longer connect with Digest authentication on Windows 10 PCs. I'm seeing the same issue this individual posted the other day on the Microsoft Docs website.
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/93105/httpclienthandler-does-not-work-for-authentication.html

The same code works fine on my Android, iOS, & Windows 10 Mobile devices. To take it a step further, the exact same UWP appxbundle that works on my Windows 10 Mobile Phone, does not work on my Windows 10 PC.

This is specific to only the UWP HttpClientHandler. On my Windows 10 PC, the HttpClientHandler in .NET Framework 4.8 still works fine.

Like I said, this is a new issue. The System.Net.Http.HttpClientHandler on UWP definitely did support Digest up until about a week ago.

My appxbundle was built with Target version 10.0.17134, Min version 10.0.15063.

I also tested with the latest & the problem still persists; Target version 10.0.18362, Min version 10.0.18362.

DOES NOT WORK
-------------------
UWP on Windows 10 Pro 2004 19041.508

WORKS
--------
UWP on Windows 10 Mobile 1709 10.0.15254.556
.NET Framework 4.8 on Windows 10 Pro 2004 19041.508
Android
iOS

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Preserve existing newlines in unchanged complex trivia
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Preserve existing newline sequences in complex-trivia whitespace when the formatter would otherwise change only the newline encoding.

Tab-indented comments take the complex-trivia formatting path even when correctly formatted. That path regenerates whitespace using the configured newline, which defaults to the platform newline. On Windows this can introduce CRLF into an otherwise LF file and produce IDE0055 diagnostics without any indentation change.

The shared trivia formatter now preserves original non-elastic whitespace when its spacing and line structure already match the desired output, ignoring only EOL encoding. Both text-change and syntax-trivia outputs use this path. Genuine indentation, spacing, trailing-whitespace, and line-count changes, as well as elastic whitespace, continue to use the preferred newline.

This follows the existing ordinary-whitespace behavior: `end_of_line` controls generated or rebuilt whitespace, rather than requiring the core formatter to normalize every existing newline.

Related: dotnet/vscode-csharp#6817.

## Tests

- Added permanent C# coverage for matching and opposite LF/CRLF preferences, default options, tabs/spaces, mixed line endings, genuine corrections, inserted newlines with and without comments, and elastic whitespace.
- Added VB regression coverage for matching and opposite LF/CRLF preferences.
- Verified the newline-preservation regressions fail against the unfixed implementation and pass with the fix. Tests cover text-change and syntax-trivia output.
- C# workspace formatting tests: 730 passed, 1 existing skip.
- VB workspace formatting tests: 229 passed.
- Both affected test projects built successfully with `RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`.
- Repository whitespace formatting verification and `git diff --check` passed.
- A 48-case probe using locally built assemblies confirmed that actual IDE0055 analysis no longer reports correctly formatted comment whitespace solely for an EOL mismatch, while genuine corrections still produce diagnostics and preferred-EOL output.

Validation ran on Windows with .NET 10. No live VS Code LSP-host or .NET Framework test run was performed. Builds reported existing package-vulnerability warnings.

Issues.Title: FBA: Fix unreliable DTBs of `#:ref` target projects
Issues.Body:
Fixes an issue reported on Teams by @DamianEdwards

This might have been a regression introduced by #84139, though I’m not certain.

https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/65d349930a64a00fb6588bd0dc17e41f05993781/src/Workspaces/MSBuild/BuildHost/Build/ProjectBuildManager.cs#L226
 
It looks like because we are not creating an intermediate `MSB.Evaluation.Project`, but instead going straight to `ProjectInstance`, the full `projectRootElement` does not get explicitly retained in the `_projectCollection`.
 
Then here: https://github.com/dotnet/msbuild/blob/4f3669e6c4d4f1aaaf2bd52eed8337a2c0f9fe52/src/Build/Evaluation/ProjectRootElementCache.cs#L290

I believe what is happening is: msbuild might need the `projectRootElement` holding the referent project of the `#:ref` later, in order to load it. But depending on whether it was in cache (see `_strongCache`/`_weakCache` fields), it might end up going to disk to look for it. It's an in-memory project though, so going to disk won't work, and will result in the failure Damian observed. The failure is nondeterministic and seems more likely to occur when lots of different projects are being loaded.

I fixed this by explicitly creating an `Evaluation.Project` and loading that into the `_projectCollection`. This has the effect of explicitly retaining the `projectRootElement`.

One issue here is I don't think these get unloaded. Some investigation is needed to find the appropriate point at which to unload, I believe it is not the Dispose method of the containing type where the impl change was made.

But, it doesn't look like our MSBuildHost dealt with unloading at all until recently, so perhaps we can live without unloading of in-memory projects for the short term.
 
I think in the medium/long term we should talk to msbuild about our practice of building projects which don't exist on disk. We should set things up so it's easier to verify things are correct "by construction".

---

I was able to verify that the new test failed reliably before the change and passes afterwards.

I opted not to add an explicitly FBA/end-to-end test as exposing the ability to clear the cache in the remote msbuild host at the right time to repro the bug seemed excessively difficult. Instead I am just testing in MSBuildHost tests "locally".

Issues.Title: Preserve generated document query parameters through URI serialization
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Construct source-generated document URIs from logical components so they survive normal vscode-uri parsing and serialization.

The generated-document query has two distinct escaping layers: parameter values are escaped first, and the complete parameter string is then assigned as the logical URI query component. Normal URI serialization escapes that component. Deserialization reads `ParsedUri.Query` to remove the URI layer before `HttpUtility.ParseQueryString` removes the parameter-value layer.

- Add a component-based `ParsedUri.From` factory using the existing normalization, validation, and encoding implementation.
- Use it to construct source-generated document URIs without prematurely decoding parameter escapes.
- Preserve regression coverage for direct and default-client roundtrips, special characters, Unicode, and optional generator assembly paths, plus factory formatting and validation.

This supports the default URI serialization change in https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-csharp/pull/9921. No legacy-client compatibility fallback is included. Clients using `toString(true)` still work for ordinary names but are not universally compatible: values containing ampersands, plus signs, or literal percent escapes can be corrupted.

## Verification

- Before the fix, all ten new-client regression cases failed with `Could not get documentId` after normal client serialization; after the fix, they pass.
- Focused tests after removing legacy-client characterization coverage: **189 passed, 1 skipped** (existing Unix-only case on Windows):
  ```
  dotnet test src\LanguageServer\ProtocolUnitTests\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.Protocol.UnitTests.csproj -f net10.0 --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SourceGeneratedDocumentUrisTests|FullyQualifiedName~ParsedUriTests" -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true --verbosity quiet
  ```
- Analyzer-enabled builds succeeded for the runnable language server and the shared Protocol project's `netstandard2.0` target. Existing dependency vulnerability warnings remain.
- Changed files formatted with `dotnet format whitespace`; `git diff --check` passes.
- End-to-end: vscode-csharp's `sourceGenerator.integration.test.ts` test **"Navigates to reference in source generated file"** passed against the locally built server through `DOTNET_ROSLYN_SERVER_PATH`, with the PR's default URI serializer (**1 passed, exit code 0**). The same test previously reproduced a timeout/server crash against the pinned Roslyn package.

Issues.Title: Limit the CA1704 numeric name exemption to type parameters
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to #85162, addressing https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/85162#discussion_r4383832691.

### Problem

#85162 exempted single-digit names from the "unmeaningful name" check so that `T1`, `T2`, … are no longer reported. Its description assumed only type parameters (`T` prefix) and interfaces (`I` prefix) could produce a bare digit after prefix stripping. Fields have their `_` prefix stripped too, so the exemption also let these through:

```csharp
class C
{
    int _1;          // no longer reported
}
interface I1 { }     // no longer reported
```

`_1` and `I1` are no more meaningful than `_c` or `ID`, which are still reported.

### Fix

The digit exemption now applies only to `SymbolKind.TypeParameter`, where `T1` is the BCL convention (`Func<T1, T2>`, `HashCode.Combine<T1, …>`):

```csharp
if (checkForUnmeaningful && symbolName.Length == 1 && !(symbol.Kind == SymbolKind.TypeParameter && IsWordNumeric(symbolName)))
```

### Tests

- `_1` added to `UnmeaningfulMembers` (field, reported)
- `I1` added to `TypeUnmeaningful_Verify_EmitsDiagnosticAsync` (interface, reported)
- The `T1`/`T2`/`T10` tests from #85162 still pass unchanged

All 76 CA1704 tests in Text.Analyzers.UnitTests pass.

### Notes for review

- This restores the behavior from before #85162 for fields and interfaces. Type parameters keep the fix.
- No rule added, removed or re-leveled, so no AnalyzerReleases entry.

Issues.Title: Introduce a new pool for large Razor tag helper collection lists
Issues.Body:
Tag helper collection builders are already pooled, but the dumps in https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Significant-intellisense-lag-when-adding/11169845 showed that there are some downsides to this, in the real world. Instead of repeatedly trimming large descriptor lists and growing them again for the next document, or missing the pool entirely due to large descriptor counts, this PR introduces a separate pool of 8 slows for large tag helper lists.

The results look good in isolation, with a downside of 2mb of additional list storage and extra growth allocations for larger cold namespace lists. Will see what DDRITs have to say too.

Scenario | Allocated before | Allocated after
-- | -- | --
Reuse a builder with 4,096 descriptors | 49,232 B | 32 B
Reuse a builder with 8,192 descriptors | 114,792 B | 32 B
Reuse 16 pooled lists with 8,192 descriptors each | 1,836,160 B | 918,080 B
Create a namespace list with 4 descriptors | 1,080 B | 88 B
Create a namespace list with 128 descriptors | 1,080 B | 2,192 B

Issues.Title: Add JSON output to dotnet sln list
Issues.Body:
`dotnet sln list` includes headers that prevent direct consumption by automation. This change adds machine-readable output without changing the default display.

- **Output formats**
  - Add `--format <table|json>`, defaulting to `table`.
  - JSON emits a sorted array of project paths, or `[]` for empty solutions.
  - Support solution filters and `--solution-folders`.

- **CLI integration**
  - Update help text and localization resources.
  - Use source-generated JSON serialization for Native AOT compatibility.

```sh
dotnet sln source.sln list --format json
# ["App/App.csproj","Lib/Lib.csproj"]
```

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #26303
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add JSON output to dotnet sln list" (#56808)

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Distinguish Copilot CLI and VS Code agent detection
Issues.Body:
.NET 10 reports Copilot CLI as legacy `copilot` and misses VS Code agent signals. This backports the Copilot-specific detection changes without expanding unrelated detectors.

- **Detection**
  - Emit `copilot-cli` for upstream CLI signals.
  - Emit `copilot-vscode` for non-empty `COPILOT_AGENT` or `AI_AGENT=github_copilot_vscode_agent`.
  - Preserve `copilot-app` and multi-agent reporting; multiple signals for one client produce one label.

- **Behavior and compatibility**
  - Newly recognized environments inherit agent-friendly output: disabled MSBuild live-node display and MTP ANSI/progress output, independently of telemetry opt-out.
  - Document continued support for historical `copilot` labels; older data cannot reliably distinguish clients.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Cover individual signals, overlaps, empty/unrelated signals, no-agent environments, and MSBuild/MTP output effects.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #56745

Issues.Title: Installation of SDK v10.0.402 succeeds but does nothing when v10.0.403 is installed (by VS)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

We use a fixed version of the .NET SDK for some/most of our repos by using a global.json with **rollforward** set to "disabled".  Of course, we have a mechanism in place to update it for all repos :p

I recently installed version **18.11.2** of **Visual Studio 2026**, which comes with version **10.0.403** of the .NET SDK and which uninstalls version **10.0.402** of the .NET SDK.

I subsequently tried to reinstall version **10.0.402** of the .NET SDK using the standalone installer.
The installer completed almost immediately and reported success, but did not install version **10.0.402** of the SDK.

Issues.Title: Print merged MTP code coverage summaries
Issues.Body:
Fixes #56796.

## Summary

- Negotiate counts-based MTP coverage summaries independently of the existing base protocol.
- Render `Code Coverage Summary` and invariant one-decimal percentages. A multi-application `Total` comes from a successfully accepted merged artifact, never from adding or averaging overlapping application measurements.
- Require complete input-path and execution/instance/session provenance before promoting a merged total. Preserve scoped measurements for incomplete, ambiguous, failed, or cancelled runs, including cancellation hidden by aggregate/ignore policies.
- Keep controller coverage arriving after session end, distinguish fallback source identities, and apply last-write-wins metric updates without combining producers.
- Add protocol, handler, provenance, lifecycle and rendering regressions; share renderer/serializer cases with the Native AOT test closure. Regenerate localized resources and document the CI line format.

## Dependencies and compatibility

The producer contract is introduced by [microsoft/testfx#12114](https://github.com/microsoft/testfx/pull/12114). The coverage extension also needs its corresponding merged-artifact metadata update and an officially released MTP containing that API.

Those producer releases/dependency flow are required before rollout. The local candidate suffixes below are validation artifacts, not published dependencies, and are not added to SDK package manifests. Older peers keep their existing execution/artifact behavior without fabricated coverage. Coverage threshold evaluation and exit-code policy remain application-owned.

The existing supported base versions remain `1.0.0` through `1.3.0`; this does not enable the separate reverse-control protocol.

## Validation

- Full Debug redist build.
- Focused managed MTP/IPC/reporter suite: 272 passed, zero failed/skipped.
- Clean-published Native AOT coverage suite: 41 passed, zero failed/skipped.
- Real Windows x64 shipping-layout composition with genuine local packages:
  - MTP `2.6.0-preview.coverage-summary.20261027.1`.
  - CodeCoverage `18.13.0-preview.coverage-summary.20261027.2`.
  - Two applications each cover `6/12` lines of the same library; the actual merged Cobertura report and the printed total both report `12/12 = 100.0%`, not the per-application `50.0%`.
  - All 11 composed cases / 38 checks pass: single/multi-app, opt-out, no coverage, failure exit `2`, zero-result exit `8` with the actual `0/12` coverage, cancellation parity, originals retained, and managed/Native AOT `--test-modules` parity.
- Regression sensitivity: ten first-round, eight second-round, and six final-round assertions failed on the pre-fix behavior and pass with the fixes.
- Vendored-manifest, Markdown links/anchors, and diff checks pass.

Representative repository commands:

```powershell
.\build.cmd -c Debug
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummary|FullyQualifiedName~FileArtifactMessagesSerializerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactPostProcessingManagerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationProtocolVersionTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests"
.\test\dotnet-aot.Tests\run-aot-tests.ps1 -Trx -Filter "FullyQualifiedName~CoverageSummary"
```

The composed fixture uses two MTP applications referencing the same library and exercising complementary branches. With the built redist selected, representative commands are:

```powershell
dotnet test --solution CoverageFeature.slnx --no-build --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --no-ansi --no-progress
dotnet test --solution CoverageFeature.slnx --no-build --no-artifact-post-processing --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --no-ansi --no-progress
dotnet test --test-modules "**\bin\Debug\net11.0\Feature.*.Tests.dll" --no-ansi --no-progress -- --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura
```

This is main-branch Windows x64 evidence, not ARM64 execution or servicing/backport sign-off. Existing test-dependency audit/AOT rollup warnings were not suppressed. A separate development `dn` harness smoke encountered an SDK-directory assertion before module execution; the actual shipping-muxer Native AOT module checks above pass.

Issues.Title: Reconcile outstanding MTP vendoring updates
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Reconcile all four open `area-vendored-sync` reports against the verified upstream revision `3c6614c5ae19ee4ddca55cbf9b3375bbaad3496b`.

| Report | Reconciliation |
| --- | --- |
| #56696 | Port `AssemblyRunNotSelected` and wire it to successful affected-run orchestrators that never start a TestHost. Render a neutral `No affected tests selected` status without inventing skipped tests. |
| #56697 | Render successful zero-test runs with neutral `Zero tests ran` wording instead of a green `Passed!` verdict. Preserve real failures and the SDK's authoritative aggregate exit code. |
| #56698 | Retain the already-supported `AllowZeroTests` option, clarify its contract, and document why the SDK uses final aggregate exit codes instead of the upstream in-process `HasTestSessionFailure` callback and global `ZeroTestsPolicy` option. |
| #56786 | Mirror the comment-only clarification that GitHub Actions workflow commands use informational `DisplayMessage` forwarding verbatim. |

Update each reviewed source's exact commit/blob baseline and adaptation notes, regenerate all 13 CLI localization files through `UpdateXlf`, and document the SDK-specific reporting invariant.

## Compatibility

No wire IDs, advertised protocol versions, dependency versions, or feature gates change. The existing experimental affected-test gate remains in place. Mapping collection does not emit a no-selection status; rejected/partial handshakes, help/discovery, cancellation, and unsuccessful orchestrator exits cannot become benign no-selection results. Session failures, per-module policies, ignored exit codes, and failures in other modules retain their existing exit-code semantics.

This targets `main`; it does not enable a downstream feature or introduce a producer/consumer rollout requiring a servicing backport.

## Validation

Components: bootstrap SDK `12.0.100-alpha.1.26480.102`, built SDK `12.0.100-dev` / `net12.0`, and the repository-aligned `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` package `2.6.0-preview.26519.1` (testfx revision `d25ab5d76da4d7202291e5d1af1070b5496751a9`). Confirmed that the deployed `dotnet.dll` matches the freshly built assembly before testing.

Successful managed layout build, exit **0**:

```powershell
$env:DOTNET_ADD_GLOBAL_TOOLS_TO_PATH = '0'
$env:DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT = '1'
& .\eng\build.ps1 /p:PublishAot=false /p:_ShouldPublishDotnetAot=false /m:1 /bl:artifacts\log\vendoring-layout.binlog /v:minimal
```

This machine lacks the MSVC/C++ prerequisites, so local verification disables native publishing. Native AOT publishing is not claimed; the changed command implementation is managed. Serial building also avoids concurrent managed/AOT projects writing the same XLF files.

Focused runner, exit **0**: **176 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**.

```powershell
$filter = 'FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationActionQueueTests|FullyQualifiedName~RunAffectedTestsWithoutTestHost_ReportsSelectionAndSummary|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestSessionFailure_ShouldNotReportPassedSummary|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithNoTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeZeroTests|FullyQualifiedName~RunNoTestsHonorsIgnoredExitCodeFromExplicitConfigurationFile|FullyQualifiedName~RunTestProjectWithTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeSuccess|FullyQualifiedName~RunMultipleTestProjectsWhereOneRanZeroTests_ShouldReturnExitCodeSuccess|FullyQualifiedName~RunAllSkippedTestsHonorsZeroTestsAndIgnoreExitCodePolicies'
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter $filter
```

The new composed-product tests use a real MTP execution orchestrator, its command-line registration, and the actual named-pipe transport—not mocked SDK handlers. They verify affected-run and mapping-collection success (host/parent exit `0`), nonzero orchestrator failures (`1`), a zero-test orchestrator exit without a TestHost (`8` becomes parent failure `1`), and framework session creation/closure failures (`10`). Existing cases cover ordinary successes, unexpected empty runs, strict/ignored zero-test policies, and mixed empty/passing modules. Unit cases retain legacy, partial/rejected handshake, discovery/help, and cancellation boundaries.

Additional successful checks:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj /t:UpdateXlf /p:Configuration=Debug /p:TargetFramework=net12.0 /nologo /v:minimal /bl:artifacts\log\vendoring-update-xlf.binlog
python .github\scripts\check_vendored_files.py validate
git diff --check
```

Verified all four upstream blob identities, preserved source indexes and unrelated manifest entries, checked all generated localization entries, and resolved all local links in the changed guidance. Retained test artifacts: `artifacts\log\test-runs\dotnet.Tests\20261027-125533-81972\test-results.trx` and `build.binlog`; layout/localization binlogs are at the paths above.

Issues.Title: [.NET 11 breaking] `dotnet test path\toprojectdir` fails
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

`dotnet test .\test\ProjectDir\` works on .NET 10 SDK but fails on the .NET 11 SDK.

### Steps to reproduce

```
git clone git@github.com:AArnott/Nerdbank.MessagePack.git
cd Nerdbank.MessagePack

# Test .NET 10 SDK
git checkout b13b65ef640a83f166ddf16eb5bffbb74159bd77
dotnet test .\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\

# Test .NET 11 SDK
git checkout 009fc86ccc9208e90f9f9e35e68eaa13caedfa38
dotnet test .\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\
```

### Expected behavior

`dotnet test` runs on both SDK versions.

### Actual behavior

.NET 10 succeeds.
.NET 11 fails:

> Unhandled exception: The project file could not be loaded. Could not find a part of the path 'G:\src\Nerdbank.MessagePack\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests.csproj'.  G:\src\Nerdbank.MessagePack\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests.csproj

Note the path doubling. Although the current directory is `G:\src\Nerdbank.MessagePack` and I specified `test\Nerdbank.MessagePack.Godot.Tests` as the relative path to the project directory, the path it expects the project at has the relative path _twice_ is the absolute path.

### Is this a regression?

Yes. .NET 11 regression relative to .NET 10.

### Are there any workarounds?

Yes: switch to the test project directory and run `dotnet test` without a path argument.

Issues.Title: dotnet test (MTP) should print the Code Coverage Summary, from the merged artifact when several test apps run
Issues.Body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

When a Microsoft.Testing.Platform test app runs directly with Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage, the platform prints the coverage summary added by RFC 019 (microsoft/testfx#9896):

```
  Code Coverage Summary:
    Total - Line: 98.9%
```

Under `dotnet test` the summary is not printed at all. #56598 says this is intentional for now: "CoverageScopeSummary and TestCoverageThresholdMessage have no representation in the SDK's `dotnet test` IPC contract."

That leaves CI systems that read coverage from the job log with nothing to read. GitLab, for example, takes its coverage percentage (merge request widget, badge, coverage history) only from a regex over the job log (https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/yaml/#coverage), so every GitLab pipeline running MTP tests has to parse the Cobertura report itself to print a total.

Measured with xunit.v3 4.0.2, Microsoft.Testing.Platform 2.5.1 (and 2.5.2-preview.26526.10) and Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage 18.12.0, on a solution with two test projects, running `dotnet test --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura`, with and without `--output detailed`:

- SDK 10.0.300 and 10.0.403: two per-project Cobertura reports, no summary.
- SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148: artifact post-processing writes `merged/merged-<id>.cobertura.xml` (line-rate 0.989, the same as `dotnet-coverage merge`), but still no summary.
- One test app run directly (`UseMicrosoftTestingPlatformRunner=true`): `Code Coverage Summary: Total - Line: 98.9%`.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Carry the RFC 019 coverage messages over the dotnet test IPC and render the Code Coverage Summary in the run summary, as the test app's own terminal output does.

For a run with several test applications, take the total from the merged coverage data that artifact post-processing already produces, not from adding up the per-application counts: test projects that load the same assembly each report it. In the solution above, the two test projects reported 6.45% and 98.9% of the same library, and the merged report says 98.9%. Per-application lines are welcome in addition, but the merged "Total" line is the one CI tools need.

A stable, documented line format (for example Total - Line: 98.9%) would let CI systems match it with a regex.

### Alternatives you've considered

- Parsing the root `line-rate` of the (merged) Cobertura report in a CI script and printing it. It works, but every pipeline re-implements it, and .NET writes small rates in exponent notation (`5E-05`), which a naive script misses.
- ReportGenerator with `-reporttypes:TextSummary`: an extra tool, it writes the summary to a file rather than to the log, and for the same two reports it computed 99.2% (254 of 256 lines) where the collector, `dotnet-coverage merge` and the SDK 11 merge all say 98.9% (184 of 186).
- Running the test apps directly instead of `dotnet test`: loses the solution-level run and the merge.

### Additional context

- microsoft/codecoverage#233 (closed): the summary is available when the test executable runs directly.
- microsoft/codecoverage#234 and #55940: one merged coverage artifact across test applications in `dotnet test` (SDK 11).
- #56598: the coverage summary is not ported to the SDK's terminal reporter.

Issues.Title: add CA2029: do not set the apartment state of a running thread
Issues.Body:
fixes dotnet/runtime#78502

CA2029 warns on `[STAThread]` on an async method or a method that is not the entry point, and on `Thread.CurrentThread.SetApartmentState(ApartmentState.STA)`, as the api review asked. setting it on a new thread before `Start` is not reported.

tested: new C# and VB tests, and a run over dotnet/runtime and dotnet/roslyn. the only hits are three tests in `ThreadTests.cs` that call it on purpose to check that it throws.

Issues.Title: Fix TemplateVerifier CLI outside test runners
Issues.Body:
🤖 This PR is part of the weekly test issue cleanup effort.

Fixes the TemplateVerifier CLI failure caused by routing directory verification through `Verify.XunitV3` when no xUnit test context exists. The TemplateVerifier now supplies a runner-independent Verify core adapter, while preserving the existing `DirectoryVerifier` override seam for framework-specific test integrations.

The authoring CLI no longer depends on `Verify.XunitV3`, and the two integration tests tracked by #53889 are re-enabled. The test also covers target-framework uniqueness so the standalone adapter preserves all supported `--unique-for` modes.

Closes #53889

Issues.Title: CLI help does not indicate `dotnet store` is deprecated while MSLearn marks `dotnet store` it as such
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

```
dotnet store -h
```

there is not clear indicator that this is deprecated. MSLearn indicates that it is. These should match.

### Steps to reproduce

`dotnet store -h`

### Expected behavior

Assuming it is deprecated, the following would work. If it is not deprecated then fix MSLearn. 

Alternatively, you could both add this to the description and mark the command as obsolete so it does not show up. 

```
Description:
  ** 
  Warning! The dotnet store command and the runtime package store feature are deprecated and no longer supported. 
  ***
  Stores the specified assemblies for the .NET Platform. By default, these will be optimized for the target runtime and
  framework.

Usage:
  dotnet store [<argument>...] [options]

Arguments:
  <argument>

Options:
  -m, --manifest <PROJECT_MANIFEST>        The XML file that contains the list of packages to be stored.
  --framework-version <FRAMEWORK_VERSION>  The Microsoft.NETCore.App package version that will be used to run the
                                           assemblies.
  -o, --output <OUTPUT_DIR>                The output directory to store the given assemblies in.
  -w, --working-dir <WORKING_DIR>          The working directory used by the command to execute.
  --skip-optimization                      Skip the optimization phase. [default: False]
  --skip-symbols                           Skip creating symbol files which can be used for profiling the optimized
                                           assemblies. [default: False]
  -f, --framework <FRAMEWORK>              The target framework to store packages for. The target framework has to be
                                           specified in the project file.
  -r, --runtime <RUNTIME_IDENTIFIER>       The target runtime to store packages for.
  -v, -verbosity <LEVEL>                   Set the MSBuild verbosity level. Allowed values are q[uiet], m[inimal],
                                           n[ormal], d[etailed], and diag[nostic].

## Local adaptation notes
Handshake/session/state string constants for the 'dotnet test' named-pipe protocol. Upstream lives in testfx IPC/Constants.cs; the SDK inlines the same constants into CliConstants.cs (TestStates, SessionEventTypes, HandshakeMessagePropertyNames, HandshakeMessageExecutionModes, HandshakeMessageHostTypes, ProtocolConstants). Watch the upstream file for added/changed wire constants. Reconciled at 868da4b6: the SDK mirrors the ArtifactPostProcessor and TestHostOrchestrator host types, the OrchestratorFeature property, and the 'tool' execution mode. The SDK consumes the retry orchestrator feature to enable retry UX before the first TestHost handshake. Issues.Title: .NET October 2026 out-of-band security updates
Issues.Body:
On October 25, 2026, we released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8.0.33, .NET 9.0.22, .NET 10.0.14, and .NET 11 Release Candidate 3 (prerelease). We recommend updating affected applications and build environments as soon as possible. .NET Framework is not affected.

## Release Notes

* [Release details and feedback](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660)
* [.NET 8.0.33 and .NET SDK 8.0.133 / 8.0.427](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.33/8.0.33.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0))
* [.NET 9.0.22 and .NET SDK 9.0.123 / 9.0.320](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.22/9.0.22.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/9.0))
* [.NET 10.0.14 and .NET SDK 10.0.114 / 10.0.403](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0))
* [.NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 and .NET SDK 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 (prerelease)](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc3/11.0.0-rc.3.md) ([Download](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0))

## Security advisories

| Advisory | Applicability | Announcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [CVE-2026-111497](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9) | Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write; all platforms when processing untrusted Brotli data. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494) |
| [CVE-2026-114148](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-r6pf-x897-gm86) | Linux archive ownership; distribution-specific ASP.NET Core archives and source-build engineering inputs. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/495) |
| [CVE-2026-70197](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-4mpw-cpwj-hxxj) | Windows sockets memory corruption; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/493) |
| [CVE-2026-102870](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-g27p-qf6j-c96c) | Standalone Blazor WebAssembly debugger packages on .NET 10/11; corrected October 13 fix. | [Announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/492) |

The October 13 updates did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870. These out-of-band updates provide the corrected fixes; the original advisory identities and revision history are preserved. For CVE-2026-102870, update the affected standalone Server/DevServer package references; updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute.

For CVE-2026-114148, affected Microsoft-published .NET 8/9 ASP.NET Core runtime and targeting-pack tarball installations require a clean replacement following the advisory. Source-built archives are build/engineering inputs, not directly deployed production runtimes. Update those inputs and recreate their extracted workspaces using ownership-controlled extraction; review and rebuild affected downstream outputs as needed. .NET 10/11 applicability is limited to source-built distributions.

Also announced at [.NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/).

Please use the [release feedback issue](https://github.com/dotnet/core/issues/10660) for release-wide issues and the linked per-CVE discussions for advisory questions.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114148 | .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in file ownership in Linux .NET tarball distributions, including ASP.NET Core runtime tarballs, ASP.NET Core targeting-pack tarballs, and source-built .NET tarballs. This advisory also provides guidance on updating affected installations and source-build engineering workflows. Incorrect ownership of runtime files installed from affected Linux tarballs can allow local elevation of privilege. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-276 (Incorrect Default Permissions) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** ARM, ARM64 and x64, as applicable to the affected Linux distribution. ## Affected Products The affected ASP.NET Core runtime, ASP.NET Core targeting-pack, and source-built .NET Linux tarballs are listed below. The installation and source-build engineering scenarios require different remediation, as described in [How do I fix the issue?](#how-fix). ### Microsoft-published ASP.NET Core archives For Microsoft-published .NET 8 and .NET 9 distributions, only the ASP.NET Core runtime and targeting-pack tarballs are affected. Other Microsoft-published .NET runtime and SDK tarballs are not included in this scope. Product | Affected version | Patched version ------- | ---------------- | --------------- ASP.NET Core 8 regular and composite Linux runtime tarballs | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.33 | 8.0.33 ASP.NET Core 8 Linux targeting-pack tarballs | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.33 | 8.0.33 ASP.NET Core 9 regular and composite Linux runtime tarballs | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.22 | 9.0.22 ASP.NET Core 9 Linux targeting-pack tarballs | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.22 | 9.0.22 These products use the archive names `aspnetcore-runtime-{version}-{rid}.tar.gz`, `aspnetcore-runtime-composite-{version}-{rid}.tar.gz`, and `aspnetcore-targeting-pack-{version}-{rid}.tar.gz`, where `{rid}` is `linux-arm`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-musl-arm`, `linux-musl-arm64` or `linux-musl-x64`. Runtime tarballs are listed on the [.NET download site](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet); targeting-pack tarballs are distributed through the .NET download CDN. ### Source-built distributions Every tarball type produced by source-build is affected in the ranges below, not only SDK tarballs. The versions in this table identify the corresponding source-build SDK release. Source-built tarballs are used in build and engineering workflows, rather than deployed directly to customer installations. Consuming an affected source-build archive does not, by itself, mean that a production shared runtime was installed from that archive. Product | Affected version | Patched version ------- | ---------------- | --------------- Source-built .NET 8 Linux distributions | >= 8.0.100, < 8.0.133 | 8.0.133 Source-built .NET 9 Linux distributions | >= 9.0.100, < 9.0.123 | 9.0.123 Source-built .NET 10.0.1xx Linux distributions | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.113 | 10.0.114-servicing.26522.126 Source-built .NET 10.0.4xx Linux distributions | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.402 | 10.0.403-servicing.26523.112 Source-built .NET 11 preview Linux distributions | >= 11.0.100-preview.1.26104.118, <= 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 | 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Review whether an installation came from an affected ASP.NET Core runtime or targeting-pack tarball, or whether a build or engineering workflow consumes an affected source-built archive. Check whether extraction preserved numeric ownership and whether the resulting files have the intended ownership. A .NET version number alone does not identify which archive was used or establish the ownership of an installation or build workspace. The vulnerability can affect installations that preserve numeric file ownership from an affected archive, for example during privileged extraction or ownership-preserving container archive import. A local account that controls the installed files or writable directories may be able to modify files used by a more privileged application. Restoring ASP.NET Core runtime or targeting-pack NuGet packages does not, by itself, introduce this tarball ownership defect. Applications using a shared runtime installed from an affected tarball can still be affected. ### How do I fix the issue? #### Customer-deployed installations For an installation made from an affected ASP.NET Core runtime or targeting-pack tarball, replace the affected installation with a clean installation from the patched distribution listed in [Affected Products](#affected-products). Updating a NuGet reference, downloading a new archive, or extracting over an existing installation does not by itself correct the existing installation. 1. Identify the affected installation directories and the applications, services, scheduled jobs, and container images that use them. Stop affected applications and services before switching installations. 2. Obtain the patched archives appropriate to your distribution, architecture, and required components from the trusted publisher. Verify their checksums against the publisher's trusted release information before extracting them. 3. Install into a **new, empty directory**, not the affected installation tree. For a shared or privileged installation, use a trusted administrator account and an administrator-controlled directory whose parent directories cannot be modified by untrusted accounts. Do not copy binaries, plugins, or other files from the affected tree into the replacement. Install any required side-by-side versions from trusted, fixed distributions. 4. Extract without restoring the archive's user/group ownership. Follow the [manual installation guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/install/linux-scripted-manual#manual-install), which uses `--no-same-owner`. For GNU tar, the following example also applies a restrictive write-permission mask: ```bash ( umask 022 tar -xzf "$PATCHED_ARCHIVE" -C "$NEW_DOTNET_ROOT" \ --no-same-owner --no-same-permissions ) ``` `PATCHED_ARCHIVE` must identify the verified patched archive, and `NEW_DOTNET_ROOT` must identify the new, empty installation directory. For a shared or privileged installation, run extraction in the trusted administrator context. Confirm that the resulting files, directories, and parent directories are controlled by the intended trusted owner and cannot be modified by untrusted accounts, including through group permissions or access-control lists. 5. Update application and service configuration to use the replacement installation, then restart and verify the applications. Check the actual runtime selected by each application, not only the version reported by an unrelated `dotnet` executable on `PATH`. Ensure that no service, scheduled job, or runtime search path still selects the affected installation. Retire the old tree using your deployment procedures, preserving evidence first if compromise is suspected. 6. Rebuild affected custom container images from trusted inputs using the patched archives and ownership-controlled extraction, and deploy replacement containers. Changing only a running container does not correct the image used to create subsequent containers. #### Source-build engineering workflows If a build or engineering workflow consumes an affected source-built tarball, update that input to the patched source-build release listed in [Affected Products](#affected-products). Recreate its extracted workspace in a new, trusted directory using ownership-controlled extraction, rather than reusing a tree extracted from the affected archive. The extraction guidance above also applies to these workspaces. Review downstream runtime or SDK packages and custom images for ownership inherited from the affected archive, and rebuild affected outputs as needed. The customer-installation steps above apply if affected outputs were actually installed or deployed; do not treat the source-build engineering archive itself as a deployed production runtime. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-111497 | .NET Brotli Decoder Out-of-bounds Write Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in the Brotli decompression library used by .NET. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory. This could lead to information disclosure, denial of service, or elevation of privilege. ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not automatically decompress Brotli data in their default configurations. Applications are exposed when they enable Brotli decompression or explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs to process attacker-controlled data, as described below. .NET Framework is not affected. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136446 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Mitigations ASP.NET Core request decompression and HttpClient automatic response decompression are not enabled by default. An application is not exposed merely because an affected .NET package is installed. Exposure requires the application to decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data through one of these paths: - Enable ASP.NET Core [automatic request decompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/aspnet/core/fundamentals/middleware/request-decompression) with Brotli (`br`) support. - Enable HttpClient automatic response decompression by configuring [HttpClientHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.httpclienthandler.automaticdecompression) or [SocketsHttpHandler.AutomaticDecompression](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.http.socketshttphandler.automaticdecompression) to include [DecompressionMethods.Brotli](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.net.decompressionmethods) or `DecompressionMethods.All`. - Explicitly use Brotli decompression APIs in `System.IO.Compression`, such as `BrotliStream` or `BrotliDecoder`. Until the update can be deployed, avoid decompressing attacker-controlled Brotli data. The following examples show how to disable Brotli decompression if you are already using it. > **Warning: Do not use these code snippets if you are not already using decompression.** Do not introduce a call to `AddRequestDecompression` if your application does not already call it. Similarly, do not introduce an `AutomaticDecompression` property assignment if your application does not already set that property. Modify only your existing decompression configuration. Enabling automatic decompression can introduce denial-of-service risks even when Brotli is excluded. If you are already using Brotli request decompression in ASP.NET Core, exclude it by removing the `br` entry from your existing decompression configuration. This retains the default gzip and deflate providers: ```csharp builder.Services.AddRequestDecompression(options => { options.DecompressionProviders.Remove("br"); }); ``` If your application already enables HttpClient automatic response decompression, disable Brotli by updating the flags on your existing handler so they do not include `DecompressionMethods.Brotli`: ```csharp var handler = new HttpClientHandler { AutomaticDecompression = DecompressionMethods.GZip | DecompressionMethods.Deflate }; var httpClient = new HttpClient(handler); ``` Applications that directly use Brotli decompression APIs must stop passing untrusted Brotli data to those APIs until updated. Ensure that other application code does not continue to decompress the same untrusted Brotli data. These changes can affect normal request and response handling and should be tested before deployment. Installing the security update remains the recommended fix. ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects .NET applications using an affected Brotli decoder in the runtime or NativeAOT packages You are affected if your application uses an affected Brotli decoder included in a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), including a decoder linked into a NativeAOT application, to decompress attacker-controlled data. See [mitigations](#mitigations) for the affected usage paths and default settings. ### How do I fix the issue? Install the updated runtime or SDK for the .NET version used by your application. If your application directly references an affected package, update that reference to the patched version listed above. .NET release | Runtime | SDK versions ------------ | ------- | ------------ .NET 8 | 8.0.33 | 8.0.133, 8.0.427 .NET 9 | 9.0.22 | 9.0.123, 9.0.320 .NET 10 | 10.0.14 | 10.0.114, 10.0.403 .NET 11 previews | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 Download .NET from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.33 Runtime or .NET 8.0.133 or 8.0.427 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.22 Runtime or .NET 9.0.123 or 9.0.320 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.14 Runtime or .NET 10.0.114 or 10.0.403 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. If you have deployed [self-contained applications](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments), rebuild and redeploy those applications with the updated runtime. For NativeAOT applications, update the SDK and any explicit compiler or runtime-pack references to patched versions, then republish and redeploy the application. Updating the machine's shared runtime alone does not replace a decoder already linked into a NativeAOT executable. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Net.Sockets. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. On Windows, reusing a `SocketAsyncEventArgs` instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can retain an undersized cached native address buffer, allowing an unauthenticated out-of-bounds write during `ReceiveFromAsync`. This vulnerability was disclosed in the October 13 advisory, but the fix was not included in the previous updates. This revision provides the corrected packages under the existing CVE-2026-70197. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/136445 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-787 (Out-of-bounds Write) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, < 8.0.33 | 8.0.33 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.22 | 9.0.22 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.22 | 9.0.22 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, < 9.0.22 | 9.0.22 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.14 | 10.0.14 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.14 | 10.0.14 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 10.0.0, < 10.0.14 | 10.0.14 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. The affected .NET 8 Windows packages include both CoreCLR and Mono runtime packs. The issue requires reuse of `SocketAsyncEventArgs` across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets; it is not limited to one runtime implementation. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.33 Runtime or .NET 8.0.133 or 8.0.427 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.22 Runtime or .NET 9.0.123 or 9.0.320 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.14 Runtime or .NET 10.0.114 or 10.0.403 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-102870 | ASP.NET Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability | October 25, 2026 OOB update
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger included in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server`. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.DevServer` also bundles the affected debugger. The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. An attacker-controlled value can escape the generated string literal and execute code on a developer's machine when the developer evaluates an expression during debugging. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70039 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Issues.Title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 2
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of [dotnet/core/discussions/10644](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10644). See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 2. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc2).

This is our second of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind.
